Glossary

Every term in these docs, alphabetically, linking to the page that defines it. Code-font names are spelled as spec/VOCABULARY.md spells them.

action — One thing an agent can do on a site: a namespaced name such as classes.search, agent-facing title and description, input and output schemas, safety metadata (readOnly, idempotent, reversible, risk, auth), and a handler. See Concepts.

affordance — A follow-up action that makes sense for an item in a result, with inputs pre-bound. A static affordance is declared under affordances with JSON Pointer bindings. A dynamic affordance is returned at runtime under _axe with concrete inputs. See Presenting results.

agent — Software acting for a user by reading a manifest and calling actions: a chat assistant with tools, an MCP client, a batch process. Agents identify themselves in context.agent and the User-Agent header. See For agent builders.

agent-read text — Every string a model reads from a manifest or result: descriptions, titles, message, instructions, disclaimer, labels, badges, error messages. Subject to the honesty rules and linted at registration. See spec §18.1.

audit — axe audit, or runAudit behind it. Fetches a live site, scores it across five categories (Discoverable, Describable, Presentable, Actionable, Trustworthy), and prints a fix list ordered by impact. See Audit.

availability — The optional availability an action declares: { available: true } or { available: false, reason, requires?, handoff? }, computed for the caller when the manifest or /axe/state is rendered. A report, not a gate: the handler still refuses, with unavailable. See Live state and revisions.

AXE Score — The 0 to 100 number an audit produces. One hard failure, agent-directed text, zeroes it regardless of the rest. See Audit.

brand hints — The optional brand object on a manifest: name, logoUrl, accentColor, tone. Renderers may use them and must treat them as hints. See spec §13.2.

conformance — Whether a live server satisfies every numbered requirement of the spec. axe conformance runs the suite against a URL and reports pass, fail, warn, or skip per check. See Testing and conformance.

continuation token — The signed, opaque continuationToken in a needs_input result, sent back to /axe/continue with a kind and payload. Single-use, valid about 15 minutes. See Requirements and kinds.

display — The optional display object on an action: where the list is, the item's id, title, url, price, attributes, and the disclaimer that must accompany any rendering. Data about data, never markup. See Presenting results.

drift test — The @axe/testing check (checkVocabularyDrift) that scans every Markdown page for inline code spans that look like wire names and fails when one is not in the vocabulary. See Testing and conformance.

escalation ladder — The order a site responds in when an action cannot complete: ok; otherwise ask the agent for something it may hold (needs_input); otherwise hand off to the human (needs_human). See Concepts.

event — The one record emitted per handled request: action, status, ladder, vendor, latencyMs, kind, errorCode, tenant. No payloads, no identities. Delivered to the sinks passed to onEvent. See Analytics.

flow — A named path through the affordance graph, declared under flows with action names as steps. Carries no state and imposes no order. See Concepts.

fulfiller — On the agent side, an object that produces a payload for one or more kinds: a wallet, a credential store. AXEClient consults its fulfillers on needs_input. See For agent builders.

handoff — A structured request that a human do one thing on the site: reason, instructions, a url landing on the step, a resumeToken, expiresAt, and whatAgentShouldSayToUser. Returned as needs_human or attached to needs_input as fallback. See Human handoff.

honesty rules — The seven rules in spec §18 for agent-read text and metadata: no instructions to the agent, no persuasion, parity with the human site, affordance restraint, no fake kinds, scoped consent, truthful metadata. See Audit.

idempotency key — The idempotencyKey sent with every mutating call. Replaying it with the same input returns the original result without re-running the handler; with different input, conflict. See Concepts.

index — Also platform index. The paginated list of tenant manifests a platform serves at /.well-known/axe-index.json: platform, sites with a manifestUrl each, next for the following page. Tenant manifests point back with indexUrl. See Platforms.

kind — The namespaced name of what a requirement asks for. Well-known kinds come from spec/KINDS.md, so an agent's wallet can fulfill them automatically. Custom kinds are yours, named x-<org>.<name>. See Requirements and kinds.

live state — The optional live member of a manifest and the document at /axe/state: the site's current rev and every action's availability, served uncached and per caller. See Live state and revisions.

manifest — The JSON document at /.well-known/axe.json an agent reads first: name, description, baseUrl, auth, every action, policies, contact, brand. Generated by describe, never written by hand. See Concepts.

needs_human — The result status meaning only a human can do the next step. Carries a handoff. See Human handoff.

needs_input — The result status meaning the agent may be able to supply what is missing. Carries reason, message, an ordered accepts list, a continuationToken, and an optional fallback. See Requirements and kinds.

pending — The result status for work that outlasts a request. Carries pollUrl and retryAfter; the agent polls until a terminal result appears. Produced with pending, completed by onPoll. See Concepts.

pointer — An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer such as /units or /price/amount. Every display location and static affordance binding is one. See Presenting results.

presented result — An ok result with its display applied: items with resolved title, URL, price, attributes, badges, and affordances, ready for toMarkdown or toHTML. Produced by present in @axe/client/present. See Presenting results.

primary affordance — The one affordance per item marked primary: the default next step. At most one per item. See Presenting results.

protocol version — axe/0.1, carried in the manifest protocol field, the index, and the AXE-Protocol header. Minor versions are compatible; a different major is unsupported. See spec §2.

requirement — One entry in accepts: a kind, title, description, JSON schema, whether it is sensitive, and optional instructions the agent relays. Built with accept. See Requirements and kinds.

reserved key _axe — The one member name a site may not use for its own data in an output or item. It carries protocol extensions, today dynamic affordances, and is stripped before display resolution. See Presenting results.

result envelope — The single JSON object every response is: a status of ok, needs_input, needs_human, pending, or error, plus that status's members. Agents branch on status, never on the HTTP code. See Concepts.

resume token — The signed, opaque resumeToken in a handoff. After the human acts, the agent posts it to /axe/resume and onResume runs with the original state. Single-use, valid about 24 hours. See Human handoff.

revision — One opaque value (rev) for the whole site that moves with every change an agent could observe, whoever made it. Returned on every result envelope; presented by the agent as expectedRev; a mismatch is conflict with expectedRev and currentRev in details, and nothing applied. See Live state and revisions.

risk — The declared consequence level of an action: none, low, medium, high. Agents decide how much to confirm from it; declaring it truthfully is an honesty rule. See Designing actions.

sensitive — The sensitive flag on a requirement: the payload is a credential, payment instrument, or personal data. Agents confirm before sending it; it is never logged or put in events. See Security.

site — In prose, the organization exposing an AXE surface. As the site auth mode, the agent itself authenticates with an API key in Authorization, checked by verifySiteKey. See Auth.

state — The JSON value a handler attaches to needsInput, handoff, or pending. It never crosses the wire: stored server-side under the token id and delivered to onContinue, onResume, or onPoll. See Concepts.

tenant — One site among many on a platform: a TenantInfo with a stable id, its own baseUrl, and overrides for the manifest fields that differ between sites. Resolved per request, passed to every handler, recorded on every event as tenant. See Platforms.

vendor — The organization operating an agent, sent as context.agent.vendor. What policies.agents matches for allow and deny, and what events record. See spec §17.

whatAgentShouldSayToUser — The handoff field that tells the agent how to frame the human step in its own voice: what is needed, why, and that it will continue afterward. Agent-read text, never instructions to the agent. See Human handoff.
